briefdescription.para: Parses expr into an AST.

detaileddescription.para: The grammar follows Python operator precedence for the supported subset of operators: +, -, *, //, %, ^ (max), & (min), unary +/-, parentheses, and function calls with comma-separated arguments.

Operator precedence (low to high):
^ (BitXor / max)
& (BitAnd / min)
+, -
*, //, %
unary -, +
atoms (constants, names, parenthesised sub-expressions, calls)

briefdescription.para: Simplifies a symbolic or numeric expression string.

detaileddescription.para:
Applies a pipeline of AST transformations twice:
CeilToIntTransformer — expands CeilToInt(x, n) to (x + n - 1) // n.
SimpleSimplifyTransformer — folds x^x → x, x + 0 → x, x * 1 → x.
MulDivCancellerTransformer — cancels common symbolic factors, e.g. 2*x//x → 2.
ExactMulDivConstantFolderTransformer — folds 1024*a//2 → 512*a.
MaxToXorTransformer — rewrites Max(a,b) and max(a,b) to a^b.
ReorderCommutativeOpsTransformer — sorts +/* operands alphabetically.
MaxIntTransformer — folds int_const ^ int_const to max(a, b).
A final linear-combination visitor then collects the result as a normalised sum of symbolic terms plus an integer constant.

simplesect.para: An int64_t when the result is fully numeric, or a simplified std::string otherwise. Returns expr unchanged when it contains syntax that the parser does not recognise (e.g. "::" in ONNX node names).

briefdescription.para: Returns the non-zero coefficient map of the difference expr1 - (expr2).

detaileddescription.para: Builds the combined expression expr1 - (expr2), runs the linear-combination visitor, and returns only those variable coefficients that are non-zero. An empty map indicates that the two expressions are equal under linear arithmetic.

simplesect.para: A map from variable name (or sub-expression key) to its integer coefficient in expr1 - expr2. Zero-coefficient terms are omitted.

briefdescription.para: Evaluates expr with the variable assignments in context.

detaileddescription.para:
Supported constructs:
Signed 64-bit integer constants.
Variable references resolved via context.
Binary operators +, -, *, // (floor division), % (modulo), ^ (max), & (min).
Unary -.
CeilToInt(n, div) — ceiling division: (n % div == 0) ? n/div : n/div + 1.

parameterdescription.para: A map from variable name to its integer value.

simplesect.para: The integer result of evaluating the expression.

parameterdescription.para: if the expression has a syntax error, references an unknown variable, or contains an unsupported node type.

briefdescription.para: Returns the set of variable names referenced in expr.

detaileddescription.para: Parses expr and walks the AST to collect every Name node. If the expression has a syntax error the function returns {expr} (a set containing the original string), matching the Python reference behaviour.

simplesect.para: An unordered set of variable name strings. Contains only expr itself when parsing fails.

briefdescription.para: Renames variables in expr according to mapping.

detaileddescription.para: Also converts Max(a, b) calls to the a^b xor form before renaming. The result has all spaces removed (matching the Python reference output).

parameterdescription.para: A map from old variable name to new variable name.

simplesect.para: The renamed expression string (no spaces).

briefdescription.para: Renames variables in expression using replacements, then simplifies.

detaileddescription.para:
Applies the following pipeline in order:
Parse expression.
Rewrite Max(a, b) → a ^ b.
Apply the rename mapping.
Apply SimpleSimplifyTransformer.
Unparse and strip spaces.
Returns expression unchanged if it has a syntax error.

parameterdescription.para: A map from old variable name to new variable name.

simplesect.para: The renamed and simplified expression string (no spaces), or expression unchanged on parse failure.

memberdef.name: rename_dynamic_dimensions

briefdescription.para: Renames dynamic shape dimensions from internal names to user-visible ones.

detaileddescription.para: Frameworks such as torch.export.export produce many internal dimension names (e.g. s0, s1, …) for dynamic shapes. This function replaces them with the canonical names supplied by the user via original.

The algorithm iterates over constraints; for each entry it finds the intersection of the equivalent-name set with original, picks the lexicographically smallest match as the canonical name, and propagates it to all aliases — unless the name starts with ban_prefix.

parameterdescription.para: A map from each dimension name to the set of all dimension names that are known to be equal to it (i.e. the equivalence class).
The set of user-visible (preferred) dimension names.
Names starting with this prefix are never selected as the canonical replacement (default: "DYN").

simplesect.para: A map {internal_name → canonical_name} covering all names in original (mapped to themselves) plus every name in constraints that was successfully resolved.

briefdescription.para: Multiplies a sequence of dimensions.

detaileddescription.para: Computes the product of all elements in args. If every element is an int64_t the result is an exact integer product; otherwise the expression "(a0)*(a1)*..." is built and simplified symbolically.

parameterdescription.para: Non-empty vector of dimensions. Returns int64_t{1} for an empty vector.

simplesect.para: The product as an integer when all operands are concrete, or as a simplified string otherwise.

briefdescription.para: Adds two dimensions.

detaileddescription.para: Returns a + b as an int64_t when both are integers; otherwise builds "(a)+(b)" and simplifies.

simplesect.para: The sum.

briefdescription.para: Subtracts b from a.

detaileddescription.para: Returns a - b as an int64_t when both are integers; otherwise builds "(a)-(b)" and simplifies.

simplesect.para: The difference.

briefdescription.para: Floor-divides a by b.

detaileddescription.para: Assumes both values are non-negative (as is typical for ONNX shape dimensions). Returns a // b as an int64_t when both are integers; otherwise builds "(a)//(b)" and simplifies.

briefdescription.para: Computes a modulo b.

briefdescription.para: Returns the maximum of a and b.

detaileddescription.para: Returns max(a, b) as an int64_t when both are integers; otherwise builds "(a)^(b)" (the xor encoding of max) and simplifies.

simplesect.para: The maximum of the two dimensions.

briefdescription.para: Returns the minimum of a and b.

detaileddescription.para: Returns min(a, b) as an int64_t when both are integers; otherwise builds "(a)&(b)" (the ampersand encoding of min) and simplifies.

simplesect.para: The minimum of the two dimensions.
